chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the forearm when it is struck and broken at the wrist joint.
He said: “If the hand withers from it, and all the fingers of the hand become paralyzed, then in that there is two-thirds of the diyah, the diyah of the hand.”
He said: “And if some of the fingers are paralyzed while some remain, then for every finger that is paralyzed there is two-thirds of its diyah.”
He said: “And likewise is the ruling regarding the leg and the foot when the toes of the foot become paralyzed.”

key_terms.اَلزَّنْدِ: the wrist joint or lower arm bone area

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah ruling for a broken arm that causes paralysis of the fingers in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation for injury when a blow and fracture lead to paralysis in the hand or foot. It specifies that total paralysis of the fingers of the hand entails two-thirds of the diyah of the hand, and each paralyzed finger carries two-thirds of its individual diyah. The same ruling applies to the foot and its toes.
